subject: Post-call: FinWise load test coordination / performance SLOs
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Barnes <amelia@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps — FinWise load test coordination

Hi Amelia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled with minimal back-and-forth: 

Recap / SLOs you called out:
- Latency target: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 200ms (for 4k token avg payload)
- Throughput: target sustained 200 req/s (spikes to 350 req/s for short bursts)
- Concurrent sessions: ~500 concurrent streams
- Streaming: yes — server-to-client streaming required for partial responses; please confirm chunking/buffer sizes if you have specifics

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the exact test window(s) and the contact for infra allowlisting.
2) We provide a k6 script + test account/API keys and a short test plan.
3) FinWise infra to whitelist Redwood test IPs (listed in our follow-up) and confirm any proxy/egress requirements.
4) Run a smoke test (low ramp) followed by two full runs; share metrics (p50/p95/p99, error rates, token costs).

I'm attaching a first-pass k6 script and a short test plan (see attachments). Can you confirm the test window you'd like and whether the SLO numbers above match what you expect for validation?

I cc'd Marissa (SRE) to help with any low-level network/ingress questions.

Thanks —
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Amelia Barnes <amelia@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Zhao <tom.zhao@finwise.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps — FinWise load test coordination

Thanks Logan — that summary looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed SLOs: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 200ms. We'll validate on 4k avg token size and include a 90% streaming traffic mix.
- Test window: we prefer Wed 05 May 2027 02:00–06:00 UTC for the primary run (our infra team will be available for the window).
- Test account: please provision a test API key tied to a test account (username: finwise-loadtest@finwise.com).
- IP allowlist: I will open a ticket with our infra team to request allowlist of Redwood IPs — can you send a canonical list of egress IPs and any CIDR ranges for our security team?

We plan to run two full passes during the window: a 30-minute ramp to target, 90-minute steady at target, then a short spike run. We will capture p50/p95/p99 and payload error rates and hand the results back to you.

One ask: for streaming tests, can Redwood support chunked responses with Content-Length omitted (i.e., Transfer-Encoding: chunked)? That is how our client keeps streaming.

Appreciate it —
Amelia Barnes
Principal SRE, FinWise
amelia@finwise.com
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Barnes <amelia@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Tom Zhao <tom.zhao@finwise.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps — FinWise load test coordination

Perfect — thanks for the confirmations and the window. Action items from our side: 

- I attached an updated k6 script (k6-loadtest-script.js) parameterized for streaming and token sizes. Also attached a short test plan (finwise-test-plan-v1.pdf) and a temporary API keys file (temp-api-keys.txt).
- Redwood supports Transfer-Encoding: chunked streaming; our runtime sends events in chunked frames for streaming responses. We'll make sure the test script exercises that path.
- Redwood egress CIDRs for this test (please provide to your security team for allowlist):
  - 34.201.12.0/24
  - 34.201.13.0/24
  - 34.201.14.0/24
  - 35.45.200.8/29

- Temporary test credentials: finwise-loadtest@finwise.com -> API key: FW-TEST-XX-YY (also in temp-api-keys.txt). Keys will expire after 72 hours unless you request an extension.
- Slack escalation: I also added Marissa (cc) as SRE lead for the run — her handle is @marissa_sre if you need frantic help during the window.

Links: shared test folder and our deal record are below for tracking: 
- https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinWiseLoadTests
- https://app.hubspot.com/deal/7843

Let me know if the CIDRs above are sufficient or if your security team needs individual IPs instead of /24 ranges. We'll stand by on Wed 05 May 02:00 UTC for the smoke start.

Thanks —
Logan
From: Tom Zhao <tom.zhao@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>, Amelia Barnes <amelia@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps — FinWise load test coordination

All looks good on our side. A couple quick confirmations before the run: 

1) Please confirm the k6 script will send the same Authorization header format we use in prod (Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>) and that your runtime will accept the temp API key as configured.
2) For streaming: we will accept Transfer-Encoding: chunked; please ensure the test script verifies that partial chunks arrive within ~200ms of generation so we can validate streaming latency separately from final completion latency.
3) We have added the CIDR ranges to our allowlist request; if you could also provide a short notice to security@finwise.com with the test-start time (they requested an email) that would speed approval.

If those three items are confirmed, we will proceed with the schedule on 05 May. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

—Tom
Tom Zhao
Infrastructure Lead, FinWise
